lines: Oh come on, this flashlight is dying right in front of me.
Hey, can someone spare a battery? Mine's basically a candle now.
I swear this flashlight gets dimmer every time I look at it.
Whoever took the last battery owes me a big apology.
I'm not scared of the dark. I'm just really annoyed by it.
Nice, we're literally working in the dark now. Love that for us.
If the flashlight quits, I'm blaming you for picking this hallway.
Please tell me one of you packed spare batteries. Please.
This thing has the nerve to flicker right when I need it.
Okay, I'm not panicking, I'm just breathing really loudly.
Hold still, I'm trying to see your face and it's not cooperating.
Does anyone else's light look orange, or is it just mine?
I miss the days when a flashlight worked on the first click.
Hey, you're the only thing I can see right now. Stay close.
Ugh, the switch is stuck again. Smack it for me, would you?
Give me a second. My hands are cold and this battery is fiddly.
Found a battery! Wait, no, it's just a gum wrapper. Ugh.
If I trip over something down here, you're picking me up.
Great. The beam's down to a sad little dot. Thanks, flashlight.
I'd trade my last granola bar for one good battery right now.
Okay, that was the spare. Who's going to tell me it's fine?
We've got about ten minutes of this thing, if we're lucky.
Stop waving that light around, you're making me dizzy.
I'd honestly rather bump into walls than stare at this flicker.
You're doing great, by the way. Dark or not, you're doing great.
I put my last battery in the radio. Don't ask why.
Whoever said flashlights last forever has never met this one.
Keep your hand on my shoulder. I can't see my own feet.
Ugh, I should've checked the batteries before we left.
Fine, I'm the one who forgot to charge it. Happy now?
This is the worst flashlight we've ever found, and I love it.
We should save the light for doors. Everything else can wait.
Dark jokes aside, I really want to see where I'm stepping.
Oh no, it's making that sad clicking noise again.
Tell me a bad joke. It'll help me forget the dark.
Why is it always the battery that dies on the scary hallway?
I'll feel a lot braver with a fresh battery in my hand.
Please don't flicker, please don't flicker, please don't flicker.
Whew, it came back. Don't breathe on it, it's fragile.
You owe me a snack for this, and I want the good kind.
I was almost brave for five whole seconds. Then the light went out.
Anyone got a battery? I'd even take one that's mostly dead.
Sorry, I'm whispering. The flashlight makes me feel watched.
My flashlight is older than both of us and way crankier.
I'm not crying. My eyes just really hate this dim beam.
This is fine. Totally fine. Just a flashlight dying in the dark.
Okay, deep breath, one more click and we move on.
Hey, if you find batteries, shout. I'll come running.
Don't say you have a spare unless it's actually in your hand.
Ha. The last battery's in the vents now. Great planning, team.
I'm too tired to be scared, so you handle the scary parts.
Careful on that step. I can barely make out the edge.
My shoulder hurts from carrying this stupid lamp around.
If you ever see a battery, grab it. Don't even ask me.
Seriously, who keeps putting the cheap batteries in our kit?
Hold the light for me. I'm going to fumble this and drop it.
Honestly, the dark isn't the problem. The noises are.
A little dark never hurt anyone. Okay, maybe a little.
I'd sell my boots for a working flashlight right now.
Point that beam at the floor, please. I need to see my feet.
I'm down to one good battery and a lot of nerve.
The flashlight's sputtering again. Please hang in there, buddy.
Ugh, I hate that little clicking noise it makes.
Stop laughing. I'm not laughing. Okay, I'm laughing a little.
I think the battery's in the cubby, or maybe my other pocket.
You're my favorite person to be stuck in the dark with.
I'll be honest, I'm scared. Can you hold my hand?
We've got two flashlights, one spare battery, and a bad attitude.
Can we stop for a snack? I can't think in this dim light.
Oof, I just bumped my elbow on the rack. Thanks, dark.
Keep the beam steady. Every wobble makes my stomach flip.
Fine, I'll carry the flashlight. You carry my nerves.
That battery's older than the last three hallways combined.
I'm starting to think flashlights hate me personally.
Please, somebody find a battery before I start talking to the walls.
